question:
Seven people, A, B, C, D, E, F and G, are sitting in a straight line, facing the north.

A sits second from one of the extreme ends of the line. Only two people sit between A and B. C sits second to the right of B. Only three people sit between C and D. F sits second to the left of D. E sits at one of the positions to the right of G.

How many people sit between A and G?
solution:
Given: Seven people, A, B, C, D, E, F and G, are sitting in a straight line, facing the north.

A sits second from one of the extreme ends of the line.

Only two people sit between A and B.

C sits second to the right of B.

Only three people sit between C and D.

F sits second to the left of D.

E sits at one of the positions to the right of G.
